However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to $N \times M$ integrations when evaluating $N$ methods on $M$ benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our research map of nearly 300 real-to-simulation papers, are open source, and we invite the Real2SimHub community to build them together.

2611.34884.title: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
2611.34884.authors: Yujia Zeng, Yuxin Chen, Yuzhen Song, Runhan Huang, Chensheng Peng, Yiyang Shao, Koushil Sreenath, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Yilun Du
2611.34884.abstract: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from individual human demonstrations. We present FineDex, a framework that makes finger-level intent both expressible and executable. FineDex learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions on hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects. To bridge generation and execution, FineDex leverages generated interactions as actionable priors for an agent that discovers physically feasible contact strategies through practice in a physics-based digital twin. By adapting at test time without per-instance retraining, FineDex generalizes across fine-grained instructions and object configurations. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art HOI generation quality and fine-grained controllability, substantial improvements in dexterous manipulation success, and successful deployment on a real dexterous humanoid robot.

2611.34914.title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
2611.34914.authors: Agelos Kratimenos, Kostas Daniilidis, Evangelos Chatzipantazis
2611.34914.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are capable low-level controllers, but they tie where objects go to the layouts they were trained on: when objects are moved or obstacles block the way, they carry them to the wrong place or into collisions. Fine-tuning on new layouts needs robot data for each one and erodes skills the model already has. We introduce Cairn, which keeps the VLA frozen and steers it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the object in its gripper. A small prior reads point clouds of the scene and the held object, along with its pose when grasped and the instruction, and samples SE(3) trajectories up to its release that lead it around obstacles and turn it to fit through gaps. The prior and the VLA form the two levels of a hierarchical planner in which feedback runs both ways: the VLA's intended motion chooses and reshapes the trajectories, and the chosen one guides the VLA's denoising. Its predicted actions, mapped to the held object's poses through the grasp, are pulled toward the next waypoint, while the VLA's weights stay untouched. Across 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes with displaced objects and obstacles, Cairn raises the success rate of a frozen {\pi}0.5 from 24.5% to 95.1%, above that of a {\pi}0.5 fine-tuned on our training layouts, without hurting standard LIBERO. On the third-party LIBERO-PRO benchmark, it raises success from 27.3% to 38.0%, and from 54.4% to 81.1% on the episodes it steers. On a real Franka, with a prior trained purely in simulation, it guides the frozen DROID {\pi}0.5 around an obstacle and to a placement at the limit of the arm's reach, where it otherwise fails. All code, models and data will be made public.

2611.34935.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
2611.34935.authors: Xueyang Yu, Yifan Jing, Taiming Lu, Linrong Cai, Zhipeng Cai, Yunyang Xiong, Gabriel Sarch, Zhuang Liu
2611.34935.abstract: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.

2405.09707.title: Point2SSM++: Self-Supervised Learning of Anatomical Shape Models from Point Clouds
2405.09707.authors: Jadie Adams, Mokshagna Sai Teja Karanam, Shireen Elhabian
2405.09707.abstract: Correspondence-based statistical shape modeling (SSM) stands as a powerful technology for morphometric analysis in clinical research. SSM facilitates population-level characterization and quantification of anatomical shapes such as bones and organs, aiding in pathology and disease diagnostics and treatment planning. Despite its potential, SSM remains under-utilized in medical research due to the significant overhead associated with automatic construction methods, which demand complete, aligned shape surface representations. Additionally, optimization-based techniques rely on bias-inducing assumptions or templates and have prolonged inference times as the entire cohort is simultaneously optimized. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Point2SSM++, a principled, self-supervised deep learning approach that directly learns correspondence points from point cloud representations of anatomical shapes. Point2SSM++ is robust to misaligned and inconsistent input, providing SSM that accurately samples individual shape surfaces while effectively capturing population-level statistics. Furthermore, we present extensions of Point2SSM++ tailored for dynamic spatiotemporal and multi-anatomy scenarios, showcasing the broad versatility of the framework. Through extensive validation across diverse anatomies, evaluation metrics, and clinically relevant downstream tasks, we demonstrate Point2SSM++'s superiority over existing state-of-the-art deep learning models and the traditional approach. Point2SSM++ substantially enhances the feasibility of SSM generation and significantly broadens its array of potential clinical applications.

2501.03095.title: A Structure-Agnostic Multi-Objective Evolutionary Weight-Sharing Compression Framework for Deep Neural Networks
2501.03095.authors: Rasa Khosrowshahli, Shahryar Rahnamayan, Beatrice Ombuki-Berman
2501.03095.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have large parameter sets that are costly to store and to deploy on resource-constrained devices. Weight-sharing compression replaces the many distinct weight values of a network with a small codebook of shared values, called codewords. Prior methods build the codebook by clustering, typically with K-means, which is expensive on models with millions of parameters and must be refit for every codebook size. To stay tractable, clustering is often applied per layer, which requires the network's layer boundaries, tensor shapes, and channel counts. We propose Uniform-Binned Entropy-Constrained Scalar Quantization (UB-ECSQ) with NSGA-II, a retraining- and gradient-free, structure-agnostic, multi-objective compression framework that treats the network as a closed-box. It flattens all parameters into a single vector that shares one codebook. Uniform Binning Quantization (UBQ) maps the vector onto equal-width uniform bins in linear time and represents each occupied bin by its centroid. Entropy-Constrained Scalar Quantization (ECSQ) then merges neighboring bins, trading the added distortion against the entropy of bin occupancy. Dynamic programming finds the optimal merge from bin statistics alone, without any forward or backward pass. NSGA-II searches over only two variables, the number of bins and the merge ratio, and returns a Pareto front of compressed models that trade accuracy against compression ratio (CR). Within a 1% drop in accuracy, and averaged over five seeds, our Pareto fronts reach CRs of 20.8 and 12.9 for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, 10.4 to 12.3 for ResNet-18/34/50/101 on ImageNet-1K, 18.4 for VGG16-BN, and 9.0 for ViT-B/16. At this budget, our framework attains a higher CR than every baseline evaluated in each setting. Over the whole objective space, our final Pareto front also achieves the highest hypervolume in all eight settings.

2501.10600.title: Wall-to-Wall Amazon Forest Height Mapping with Planet NICFI, Aerial LiDAR, and a U-Net Regression Model
2501.10600.authors: Fabien H. Wagner, Ricardo Dalagnol, Griffin Carter, Mayumi C. M. Hirye, Shivraj Gill, Le Bienfaiteur Sagang Takougoum, Samuel Favrichon, Michael Keller, Jean P. H. B. Ometto, Lorena Alves, Cynthia Creze, Stephanie P. George-Chacon, Shuang Li, Zhihua Liu, Adugna Mullissa, Yan Yang, Erone G. Santos, Sarah R. Worden, Martin Brandt, Philippe Ciais, Stephen C. Hagen, Sassan Saatchi
2501.10600.abstract: Tree canopy height is a key indicator of forest biomass, productivity, and structure, yet measuring it accurately at regional or larger scales, whether from the ground or remotely, remains challenging. The objective of this study is to generate the first complete canopy height map of the Amazon forest at $\sim$4.78 m resolution using Planet NICFI imagery and deep learning. Specifically, we (i) trained a U-Net regression model with canopy height models (CHM) derived from tropical airborne LiDAR and their corresponding Planet NICFI images to estimate canopy height, (ii) evaluated the accuracy of our map against existing global products based on Sentinel-2/1 and Maxar Vivid2 imagery, and (iii) assessed its capacity to capture small-scale canopy height changes. Tree height predictions on the validation sample had a mean absolute error of 3.68 m, with minimal systematic bias across the full range of tree heights in the Amazon forest. The main biases are a slight overestimation (up to 5 m) for heights of 5-15 m and an underestimation for most trees above 50 m. Outperforming existing global model-based canopy height products in this region, the model accurately estimated canopy heights up to 40-50 m with minimal saturation. We determined that the Amazon forest has an average canopy height of $\sim$22 m (standard deviation $\sim$5.3 m) and exhibits large-scale patterns, ranging from the tallest forests of the Guiana Shield to shorter forests along wetlands, rivers, rocky outcrops, savannas, and high elevations. Events such as logging or deforestation could be detected from changes in tree height, and the results demonstrated a first success in monitoring the height of regenerating forests. Finally, the map of the Amazon forest canopy height is displayed.

2503.11006.title: Fine-Grained Instruction-Guided Graph Reasoning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
2503.11006.authors: Yaohua Liu, Binkai Ou, Xinyuan Song, Rong Fu, Amir H. Gandomi, Simon Fong
2503.11006.abstract: Vision and Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to traverse complex environments by following natural language instructions, demanding accurate alignment between visual observations and linguistic guidance. To address these challenges, we propose a fine grained instruction guided graph reasoning framework (FIGR) that enhances both spatial representation and instruction understanding during navigation. Specifically, an observation graph interaction mechanism is introduced to disentangle angular and visual cues while strengthening directed edge representations through geometric embedding, enabling more reliable spatial reasoning within the navigation graph. The key detail guidance module is implemented as Adaptive Open Vocabulary Guidance (AOVG), where a contextual role parser dynamically identifies location, object, spatial relation, and other contextual cues. This design avoids exact string matching and supports previously unseen entities and compositional expressions. For multilingual instructions, a Multilingual Semantic Adapter (MSA) maps language-specific representations into a shared navigation-semantic space. By jointly integrating structured graph reasoning with instruction critical semantic cues, the proposed approach significantly improves the agent ability to follow complex navigation instructions. On the validation-unseen splits, FIGR achieves 67 SPL on R2R and 64.8 sDTW on RxR, exceeding SPENav by 1 percentage point in SPL and PRET by 2.4 points in sDTW, respectively.

2506.16745.title: Class Agnostic Instance-level Descriptor for Instance Search
2506.16745.authors: Qi-Ying Sun, Wan-Lei Zhao, Hui-Ying Xie, Yi-Bo Miao, Chong-Wah Ngo
2506.16745.abstract: Despite the great success of the deep features in content-based image retrieval, the visual instance search remains challenging due to the lack of effective instance-level feature representation. Supervised or weakly supervised object detection methods are not the appropriate solutions due to their poor performance on the unknown object categories. In this paper, based on the feature set output from self-supervised ViT, the instance-level region discovery is modeled as detecting the compact feature subsets in a hierarchical fashion. The hierarchical decomposition results in a hierarchy of instance regions. On the one hand, this kind of hierarchical decomposition well addresses the problem of object embedding and occlusions, which are widely observed in real scenarios. On the other hand, the non-leaf nodes and leaf nodes on the hierarchy correspond to the instance regions in different granularities within an image. Therefore, features in uniform length are produced for these instance regions, which may cover across a dominant image region, an integral of multiple instances, or various individual instances. Such a collection of features allows us to unify the image retrieval, multi-instance search, and instance search into one framework. The empirical studies on three benchmarks show that such an instance-level descriptor remains effective on both the known and unknown object categories. Moreover, the superior performance is achieved on single-instance and multi-instance search, as well as image retrieval tasks.

2507.13231.title: VITA: Vision-to-Action Flow Matching Policy
2507.13231.authors: Dechen Gao, Boqi Zhao, Andrew Lee, Ian Chuang, Hanchu Zhou, Hang Wang, Zhe Zhao, Junshan Zhang, Iman Soltani
2507.13231.abstract: Conventional flow matching and diffusion-based policies sample via iterative denoising from standard noise distributions (e.g., Gaussian), and require conditioning modules to repeatedly incorporate visual information during the generative process, incurring substantial time and memory overhead. To reduce the complexity, we develop VITA (Vision-To-Action flow matching policy), a noise-free and conditioning-free flow matching policy learning framework that directly flows from visual representations to latent actions. Since the source of the flow is visually grounded, VITA eliminates the need for visual conditioning during generation. As expected, bridging vision and action is challenging, because actions are lower-dimensional, less structured, and sparser than visual representations; moreover, flow matching requires the source and target to have the same dimensionality. To overcome this, we introduce an action autoencoder that maps raw actions into a structured latent space aligned with visual latents, trained jointly with flow matching. To further prevent latent action space collapse during end-to-end training, we propose flow latent decoding, which anchors the latent generation process by backpropagating the action reconstruction loss through the flow matching ODE (ordinary differential equation) solving steps. We evaluate VITA on 9 simulation and 5 real-world tasks from ALOHA and Robomimic. VITA achieves 1.9x faster inference compared to conventional flow matching with conditioning modules, while outperforming or matching state-of-the-art policies. Project page: https://ucd-dare.github.io/VITA/.

2508.12931.title: Towards High-Resolution Industrial Image Anomaly Detection
2508.12931.authors: Ximiao Zhang, Min Xu, Xiuzhuang Zhou
2508.12931.abstract: Current anomaly detection methods primarily focus on low-resolution scenarios. For high-resolution images, conventional downsampling often misses subtle anomalies due to the loss of fine-grained discriminative information. Although recent studies have explored lightweight networks or image tiling with ensemble strategies, they still fall short of industrial requirements for both accuracy and efficiency. To address the above issues, we propose HiAD, a general framework for high-resolution anomaly detection that identifies anomalies of varying sizes under constrained computational resources. Specifically, HiAD employs a dual-branch architecture that integrates anomaly cues across different scales to comprehensively capture both subtle and large-scale anomalies. Furthermore, it incorporates a multi-resolution feature fusion module that injects multi-scale semantic context into patch-level representations, thereby suppressing ultrafine texture variations while retaining anomaly-relevant structural details. To improve adaptability and efficiency, HiAD constructs a detector pool with an adaptive strategy selection mechanism that automatically identifies the optimal detector assignment strategy for varying input data, enabling robust anomaly detection while effectively controlling computational costs. HiAD requires neither additional supervision nor auxiliary learnable parameters and can be seamlessly integrated with a wide range of anomaly detection methods. Extensive experiments are conducted on multiple high-resolution anomaly detection benchmarks, including the specifically constructed MVTec-HD, VisA-HD, and RealIAD-HD benchmarks, as well as the existing MVTec 2 benchmark. The results consistently demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of HiAD across diverse experimental settings. The code is available at https://github.com/cnulab/HiAD.

2508.16863.title: Delta-SVD: Efficient Compression for Personalized Text-to-Image Models
2508.16863.authors: Tangyuan Zhang, Shangyu Chen, Qixiang Chen, Junyu Yan, Jingwen Ye, Jianfei Cai
2508.16863.abstract: Personalizing a text-to-image diffusion model by full fine-tuning gives the strongest subject fidelity but produces a full copy of the model per subject: a thousand personalized Stable Diffusion checkpoints approach five terabytes, so storage, not compute, is what fails to scale. We present Delta-SVD, which compresses the weight change that personalization makes rather than the model. Given only a finished checkpoint and its base, it takes a truncated SVD of each layer's weight delta and keeps the few components that carry its spectral energy, selected by a per-layer energy threshold or by a global byte budget filled by water-filling, optimal for the continuous relaxation and empirically near-optimal for discrete rank allocation. Nothing is trained and no subject image is read, so the method applies to legacy and third-party checkpoints for which training-time adapters such as LoRA were never produced. The factors merge back into dense weights at load time, so serving runs at the uncompressed model's exact latency, whereas whole-model 8-bit and 4-bit quantization slow inference by 1.5-3.4 times. On the 30-subject DreamBooth benchmark, Delta-SVD matches the uncompressed model to within 0.01 DINO at 7-fold compression and keeps 98% of its fidelity at 33-fold compression. Among post-hoc baselines, only dense-delta quantization at 411 MiB matches it; below that size Delta-SVD dominates pruning, random-rank selection, and both whole-model and dense-delta quantization on the storage-quality frontier. The same holds on 84 diverse CustomConcept101 subjects, where a 9 MiB adapter reproduces the uncompressed outputs at paired DINO 0.77, and on a fully fine-tuned SD3.5-medium MMDiT, where a 531 MB adapter matches the uncompressed model to within 0.01 DINO.

2509.16476.title: GazeVLM: Gaze-Guided Foveated Inference for Efficient Vision-Language Models
2509.16476.authors: Lei Wang, Jiawen Qi, Qinyu Chen
2509.16476.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve remarkable multimodal performance but introduce substantial computational cost due to the large number of visual tokens. Existing approaches typically rely on token pruning, sparse attention, or additional control modules, often introducing accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper presents GazeVLM, a training-free framework that leverages human gaze as a natural guidance signal for efficient inference. GazeVLM allocates computation to gaze-relevant regions through a gaze-guided region-of-interest (ROI) representation and an optional two-scale design that preserves global context. We also construct GazeVLM-VQA, to the best of our knowledge, the first real-world wearable-gaze visual question answering (VQA) dataset specifically constructed for VLM inference, containing reference images, human gaze traces, and gaze-aligned question-answer pairs. Experiments on the GazeVLM-VQA benchmark demonstrate that GazeVLM improves both answer quality and efficiency across Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and Qwen3-VL-8B models. It reduces visual tokens by up to 84.2%, prefill FLOPs by up to 92.8%, and achieves up to 11.6 times prefill speedup, while improving answer-match accuracy by up to 8.6 percentage points (pp). These results show that aligning VLM computation with human visual attention provides a promising path toward efficient VLM inference. We publicly release the GazeVLM-VQA dataset (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mdi-GezeIkmege3segUQCnvnK6P-skaw?usp=sharing).

2509.21790.title: LongScape: Advancing Long-Horizon Embodied World Models with Context-Aware MoE
2509.21790.authors: Lei Jin, Yu Shang, Yiding Ma, Xin Zhang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li
2509.21790.abstract: Video-based world models hold significant potential for generating high-quality embodied manipulation data. However, current video generation methods struggle to achieve stable long-horizon generation: classical diffusion-based approaches often suffer from temporal inconsistency and visual drift over multiple rollouts, while autoregressive methods tend to compromise on visual detail. To solve this, we introduce LongScape, a hybrid framework that adaptively combines intra-chunk diffusion denoising with inter-chunk autoregressive causal generation. Our core innovation is an action-guided, variable-length chunking mechanism that partitions video based on the semantic context of robotic actions. This aligns chunk boundaries with robotic interaction events and motion dynamics, enabling the model to flexibly generate diverse dynamics. We further introduce a Context-aware Mixture-of-Experts (CMoE) framework that adaptively activates specialized experts for each chunk during generation to produce high-quality videos with coherent chunk transitions. Extensive experiments on two embodied benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation performance. Notably, LongScape maintains high generation quality and temporal consistency over 1,000-frame rollouts. When used as synthetic training data, LongScape videos lift the success rate of a downstream VLA policy by 9.8 percentage points over real-only training, outperforming augmentation with other long-video generators. Our code is available at: https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/Longscape.

2511.17843.title: Assemble the Puzzle: Cross-Agent Utility-Aware Feature Scheduling for Bandwidth-Limited Cooperative Perception
2511.17843.authors: Chenyi Wang, Muhammad Waqar, Wujie Wen, Ming F. Li
2511.17843.abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) lets connected vehicles and roadside units detect objects beyond the inherent range limitation and occlusion of single-agent systems, yet its practicality is constrained by limited Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication bandwidth. Existing methods improve bandwidth efficiency by letting collaborating agents send only selected feature cells driven by local detection confidence, serving a centralized ego agent's request. They overlook realistic communication scheduling and neglect cross-agent redundancy. We present JigsawComm, a decentralized utility-aware feature scheduling framework that learns to ``assemble the puzzle'' of multi-agent features. Choosing who sends each region requires a utility that measures what each agent's features contribute to the collaboration. JigsawComm incorporates a lightweight feature utility estimator, learned without utility labels from the cooperative model's own leave-one-agent-out counterfactuals, which aligns utilities onto a single comparable scale across agents. From one broadcast of compact utility maps, every agent ranks the observers of each cell and sends the cells it observes best to maximize coverage and, budget permitting, second best for accuracy refinement. Each agent also broadcasts its onboard detector's lightweight bounding box list, enabling an intermediate-late hybrid fusion with our feature-anchored box consensus, which synergistically enhances the final perception results with all available observations. With every transmitted byte counted, JigsawComm at 0.45 KB per vehicle outperforms all baselines on the real-world V2X-Real benchmark, and under measured C-V2X traces on CooperScene it retains 74.5 of its 79.8 AP@0.5, at least 15.5 points above every prior art baseline.

2511.22991.title: Guiding Visual Autoregressive Models through Spectrum Weakening
2511.22991.authors: Chaoyang Wang, Tianmeng Yang, Yunhai Tong
2511.22991.abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) has become a widely adopted practice for enhancing generation quality and improving condition alignment. Recent studies have explored guidance mechanisms for unconditional generation, yet these approaches remain fundamentally tied to assumptions specific to diffusion models. In this work, we propose a spectrum weakening framework for visual autoregressive (AR) models. The method is training-free and condition-free, constructing a controllable weak model in the spectral domain without architectural modifications. Specifically, we selectively retain spectral components along the channel dimension of internal representations to weaken features without requiring a complete spatial layout. We further apply spectrum renormalization to maintain feature scales during generation. Comprehensive empirical and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of our approach, including raster-scan, random-order, and scale-wise AR, spanning discrete and continuous modeling and covering class and text-condition scenarios, demonstrating high-quality unconditional generation and strong prompt alignment for conditional generation.

2511.23113.title: db-SP: Accelerating Sparse Attention for Visual Generative Models with Dual-Balanced Sequence Parallelism
2511.23113.authors: Siqi Chen, Ke Hong, Tianchen Zhao, Ruiqi Xie, Zhenhua Zhu, Xudong Zhang, Yu Wang
2511.23113.abstract: Scaling Diffusion Transformer (DiT) inference via sequence parallelism is critical for reducing latency in visual generation, but is severely hampered by workload imbalance when applied to models employing block-wise sparse attention. The imbalance stems from the inherent variation in sparsity across attention heads and the irregular distribution of dense blocks within the sparse mask, when sequence parallelism is applied along the head dimension (as in Ulysses) or the block dimension (as in Ring Attention). In this paper, we formalize a sparse imbalance ratio to quantify the imbalance, and propose db-SP, a sparsity-aware sequence parallelism technique that tackles the challenge. db-SP contains a dual-level partitioning approach that achieves near-perfect workload balance at both the head and block levels with negligible overhead. Furthermore, to handle the evolving sparsity patterns across denoising steps and layers, db-SP dynamically determines the parallel degrees for the head and block dimensions at runtime. Experimental results demonstrate that db-SP delivers an end-to-end speedup of 1.25x and an attention-specific speedup of 1.40x over state-of-the-art sequence parallel methods on average. Code is available at https://github.com/thu-nics/db-SP.

2602.00671.title: HPC: Hierarchical Point-based Latent Representation for Streaming Dynamic Gaussian Splatting Compression
2602.00671.authors: Yangzhi Ma, Bojun Liu, Wenting Liao, Dong Liu, Zhu Li, Li Li
2602.00671.abstract: While dynamic Gaussian Splatting has driven significant advances in free-viewpoint video, maintaining its rendering quality with a small memory footprint for efficient streaming transmission still presents an ongoing challenge. Existing streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting compression methods typically leverage a latent representation to drive the neural network for predicting Gaussian residuals between frames. Their core latent representations can be categorized into structured grid-based and unstructured point-based paradigms. However, the former incurs significant parameter redundancy by inevitably modeling unoccupied space, while the latter suffers from limited compactness as it fails to exploit local correlations. To relieve these limitations, we propose HPC, a novel streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting compression framework. It employs a hierarchical point-based latent representation that operates on a per-Gaussian basis to avoid parameter redundancy in unoccupied space. Guided by a tailored aggregation scheme, these latent points achieve high compactness with low spatial redundancy. To improve compression efficiency, we further undertake the first investigation to compress neural networks for streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting through mining and exploiting the inter-frame correlation of parameters. Combined with latent compression, this forms a fully end-to-end compression framework. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that HPC substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods. It achieves a storage reduction of 67% against its baseline while maintaining high reconstruction fidelity.

2602.13022.title: Learning Image-based Tree Crown Segmentation from Enhanced Lidar-based Pseudo-labels
2602.13022.authors: Julius Pesonen, Stefan Rua, Josef Taher, Niko Koivum\"aki, Xiaowei Yu, Teemu Hakala, Eija Honkavaara
2602.13022.abstract: Mapping individual tree crowns is essential for understanding and caring for our environment by improving the accuracy of urban tree inventories and precise monitoring of forest health. However, automatically separating tree crowns in aerial imagery is challenging because of factors like complex crown textures and frequent partial overlap between neighbouring trees. We present a method to train deep learning models to segment individual tree crowns from RGB and multispectral imagery, using pseudo-labels derived from aerial laser scanning (ALS) data. We show that incorporating information from a zero-shot instance segmentation model, Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), improves model training. Our method enables training domain-specific optical image-based models without requiring manual training annotation. We trained and evaluated the models with data from an urban area in Southern Finland and compared their performance with several baselines. Our best model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 0.621 on manually delineated tree crowns in a geographically separate test area. This represents a 21% increase in mIoU over the directly evaluated SAM 2-enhanced pseudo-labels (0.513) and a 19% increase over the best image-based baseline (0.524). Incorporating SAM 2 into the pseudo-label generation process improved the best model mIoU by 9.9%, from 0.565 to 0.621, while the average mIoU across the tested models increased by 8.4%, from 0.557 to 0.604. These results highlight that automatically generated and foundation-model-enhanced pseudo-labels can provide effective domain-specific supervision for individual tree crown segmentation without manual training annotation, despite the noise in the initial ALS-based segments.

2602.16702.title: Saliency-Aware Multi-Route Thinking: Grounding and Reasoning on Vision-Language Agents
2602.16702.authors: Mingjia Shi, Yinhan He, Yaochen Zhu, Cassie Dong, Jundong Li
2602.16702.abstract: Vision-language (VL) agents increasingly combine extended reasoning with ex ternal visual tools. Yet long traces can drift from the image as generated text accumulates, while directly inserting tool outputs can turn one incorrect detection into a persistent premise. We ask how inference-time computation can improve reasoning without surrendering control to the tool. We propose Saliency-Aware Principle Selection (SAP), a training-free method that evolves compact reason ing principles rather than lengthening a single token trajectory. Each principle generates independent routes from the original image and prompt. A frozen ground ing tool scores whether objects cited along these routes are visually supported; agreement, diversity, and uncertainty further control drift, collapse, and overcon fidence. The tool supplies selection evidence but never writes the reasoning or answer. Across object-hallucination benchmarks, SAP consistently improves vi sually grounded prediction under a unified model and decoding budget. Broader evaluations spanning reasoning, knowledge, OCR, documents, diagrams, and real world imagery show that this gain does not come at the expense of general VL capability. Cross-architecture and model-scale experiments further demonstrate that the principle-selection mechanism transfers beyond a single backbone, while controlled ablations confirm that both multi-route exploration and evolutionary se lection are necessary. Because routes run in parallel, SAP also reduces serial latency relative to an equally long chain. Together, these results show that scaling over governed reasoning behaviors can preserve visual evidence more effectively than simply extending the chain.

2602.17636.title: CORAL: Correspondence Alignment for Improved Virtual Try-On
2602.17636.authors: Jiyoung Kim, Youngjin Shin, Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Jisu Nam, Tongmin Kim, Jongjae Park, Hyeonwoo Kang, Seungryong Kim
2602.17636.abstract: Existing methods for Virtual Try-On (VTON) often struggle to accurately transfer garment appearance, especially in unpaired settings where accurate person-garment correspondence is required. These methods do not explicitly supervise person-garment alignment, leaving correspondence to be learned implicitly within the generation model. In this paper, we first analyze full self-attention in DiT-based architectures and show that person-to-garment query-key matching aligned with local geometric correspondence is closely related to try-on quality. Building on this insight, we introduce CORrespondence ALignment (CORAL), a DiT-based framework that explicitly aligns query-key matching with robust external correspondences. CORAL integrates two complementary components: a correspondence distillation loss that aligns reliable matches with person-to-garment attention, and an entropy minimization loss that sharpens the attention distribution. For evaluation, we further propose a VLM-based evaluation protocol to better reflect human preference. CORAL consistently improves over the baseline, enhancing both global shape transfer and local detail preservation. Extensive ablations validate our design choices.

2603.02518.title: Beyond Anatomy: Interpreting Graph-Based ASD Classification Across ABIDE Settings
2603.02518.authors: Syeda Hareem Madani, Noureen Bibi, Adam Rafiq Jeraj, Sumra Khan, Anas Zafar, Rizwan Qureshi
2603.02518.abstract: Graph neural networks can classify resting-state functional MRI connectomes, but a high score on one configuration leaves open which representation choices matter and whether the result supports broader clinical use. We examine this problem through two ABIDE-I analyses. On a balanced 400-subject subset, an AAL-based graph convolutional network (73.3%), an MSDL-based configuration (84.0%), and a five-model graph attention ensemble (95.0%) report high nominal performance. However, we show that this 95.0% result, which substantially exceeds typical multi-site ABIDE benchmarks (65-70%), stems from a single site-stratified test split of 60 subjects and does not reflect out-of-distribution generalization to unseen acquisition centers. In a separate 1,035-subject analysis with different preprocessing and parcellation, BrainGAT reaches 58.26% mean accuracy, below an SVM at 69.37%. We interpret these as comparisons of complete pipelines and retain both the favorable ensemble result and the negative broader-cohort result. Analysis of the existing summaries shows that atlas substitution changes the number of possible region pairs approximately ninefold, that accuracy on 60 test subjects changes by 1.67 percentage points per prediction, and that the best accuracy and AUC belong to different broader-cohort classifiers. Regional attribution on the baseline GCN (not the 95% GAT ensemble) highlights default-mode-network features but reflects classifier reliance rather than validated clinical biomarkers. Unresolved metric aggregation and diagnosis-aware harmonization limit the findings to exploratory classification evidence.

2603.12409.title: ABRA: Teleporting Fine-Tuned Knowledge Across Domains for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
2603.12409.authors: Mattia Bernardi, Chiara Cappellino, Matteo Mosconi, Samuele Bertaina, Enver Sangineto, Angelo Porrello, Simone Calderara
2603.12409.abstract: Although recent Open-Vocabulary Object Detection architectures, such as Grounding DINO, demonstrate strong zero-shot capabilities, their performance degrades significantly under domain shifts. Moreover, many domains of practical interest, such as nighttime or foggy scenes, lack large annotated datasets, preventing direct fine-tuning. In this paper, we introduce Aligned Basis Relocation for Adaptation (ABRA), a method that transfers class-specific detection knowledge from a labeled source domain to a target domain where these classes have no annotations, and no images are selected for them. ABRA decouples a detector into class-agnostic domain experts, obtained through Objectification, and class-specific residuals learned on top of them, and projects each source residual onto the singular subspaces of the target domain expert, without training. Extensive experiments across challenging domain shifts demonstrate that ABRA successfully teleports class-level specialization under multiple adverse conditions. Our code is available on GitHub.

2603.19218.title: Rethinking Vector Field Learning for Generative Segmentation
2603.19218.authors: Chaoyang Wang, Yaobo Liang, Boci Peng, Fan Duan, Yunhai Tong
2603.19218.abstract: Taming diffusion models for generative segmentation has attracted increasing attention. While existing approaches primarily focus on architectural tweaks or training heuristics, there remains a limited understanding of the intrinsic mismatch between continuous flow matching objectives and discrete perception tasks. In this work, we revisit diffusion segmentation from the perspective of vector field learning. We identify two key limitations of the commonly used flow matching objective: gradient vanishing and trajectory traversing, which result in slow convergence and poor class separation. To tackle these issues, we propose a principled vector field reshaping strategy that augments the learned velocity field with a detached distance-aware correction term. This correction introduces both attractive and repulsive interactions, enhancing gradient magnitudes near centroids while preserving the original diffusion training framework. Furthermore, we design a computationally efficient, quasi-random centroid encoding scheme inspired by Kronecker sequences, which integrates seamlessly with an end-to-end pixel neural field framework for pixel-level semantic alignment. Extensive experiments consistently demonstrate significant improvements over vanilla flow matching approaches, substantially narrowing the performance gap between generative segmentation and strong discriminative specialists.

2603.24296.title: AMIF: Authorizable Medical Image Fusion Model with Built-in Authentication
2603.24296.authors: Jie Song, Jun Jia, Wei Sun, Wangqiu Zhou, Tao Tan, Guangtao Zhai
2603.24296.abstract: Multimodal medical image fusion integrates complementary anatomical and functional information from different imaging modalities, providing richer image representations for clinical interpretation and assisted diagnosis. High-performance medical image fusion models are typically built upon medical images with high data sensitivity and security requirements, together with carefully designed algorithmic architectures. Collectively, these constitute intellectual property of significant value. As fusion results are circulated and reused in scenarios such as cross-institutional collaboration, traceable copyright protection and controlled authorization for these medical fusion assets are becoming increasingly important. However, existing multimodal medical image fusion models typically generate unprotected results and lack built-in copyright protection and authorization mechanisms. Conventional post-processing watermarking is independent of the fusion model, making it difficult for copyright protection to become an intrinsic capability of the model itself. To address this issue, we propose AMIF, the first Authorizable Medical Image Fusion model with built-in authentication, which integrates authorization access control into the image fusion objective. For unauthorized usage, AMIF embeds explicit and visible copyright identifiers into fusion results. In contrast, high-quality fusion results are accessible upon successful key-based authentication.

2604.08641.title: On Semiotic-Grounded Interpretive Evaluation of Generative Art
2604.08641.abstract: Interpretation is essential to deciphering the language of art: audiences communicate with artists by recovering meaning from visual artifacts. However, current Generative Art (GenArt) evaluators primarily emphasize surface-level image quality or literal prompt adherence, failing to assess the deeper symbolic or contextual meaning intended by the creator. We formalize this observation using Peircean computational semiotic theory that models Human-GenArt Interaction (HGI) as cascaded semiosis. This framework reveals that artistic meaning is conveyed through iconic, symbolic, and indexical modes, whereas appearance-centered evaluators tend to emphasize the iconic mode. Building on this account, we propose SemJudge, an interpretation-centric evaluation framework that uses a Hierarchical Semiosis Graph (HSG) to reconstruct meaning conveyance from prompt to generated artifact. Experiments on an interpretation-intensive benchmark, SemiosisArt, show that SemJudge aligns more closely with human judgments than existing baselines. User studies further demonstrate that SemJudge produces deeper, more insightful artistic interpretations. We hope these findings pave the way for GenArt to move beyond the generation of "pretty" images toward a medium capable of understanding and expressing complex human experience. Project page: https://github.com/songrise/SemJudge

2604.19233.title: Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference for Enhanced Small Object Detection in High-Resolution Imagery
2604.19233.authors: Francesco Moretti, Yi Jin, Guiqin Mario
2604.19233.abstract: Deep learning-based object detectors have achieved remarkable success across numerous computer vision applications, yet they continue to struggle with small object detection in high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, where dense object distributions, variable shooting angles, diminutive target sizes, and substantial inter-class variability pose formidable challenges. Existing slicing strategies that partition high-resolution images into manageable patches have demonstrated promising results for enlarging the effective receptive field of small targets; however, their reliance on fixed slice dimensions introduces significant redundant computation, inflating inference cost and undermining detection speed. In this paper, we propose \textbf{Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference (ASAHI)}, a novel slicing framework that shifts the paradigm from prescribing a fixed slice size to adaptively determining the optimal number of slices according to image resolution, thereby substantially mitigating redundant computation while preserving beneficial overlap between adjacent patches. ASAHI integrates three synergistic components: (1)an adaptive resolution-aware slicing algorithm that dynamically generates 6 or 12 overlapping patches based on a learned threshold, (2)a slicing-assisted fine-tuning (SAF) strategy that constructs augmented training data comprising both full-resolution and sliced image patches, and (3)a Cluster-DIoU-NMS (CDN) post-processing module that combines the geometric merging efficiency of Cluster-NMS with the center-distance-aware suppression of DIoU-NMS to achieve robust duplicate elimination in crowded scenes. Extensive experiments on VisDrone2019 and xView, demonstrate that ASAHI achieves state-of-the-art performance with 56.8% on VisDrone2019-DET-val and 22.7% on xView-test, while reducing inference time by 20-25% compared to the baseline SAHI method.

2604.21066.title: When the Prior Is Wrong: Probing Misspecified Diffusion Priors in Inverse Problems
2604.21066.abstract: While diffusion priors generate high-quality posterior samples across many scientific inverse problems, they are often trained on purely simulated data, thus inheriting the errors and biases of these underlying sources. Many approaches to adapting diffusion priors from a single observation require sufficient conflict between the data and the prior to successfully adapt and do not allow specific misspecification hypotheses to be tested. On the other hand, existing out-of-distribution (OOD) detection methods determine whether the observation is compatible with a fixed prior, rather than specifying which assumptions to relax or by how much. To address these issues, we propose PIVOT: Prior Inference Via Observation-driven Transformations, which formulates diffusion prior misspecification as inference over an underlying latent variable representing a scientifically plausible discrepancy. By expanding the prior along these plausible directions of misspecification, PIVOT infers a posterior over the strength of each proposed discrepancy given the observation. This process can be efficiently amortized with just one posterior sampling pass using a conditional diffusion model. We also demonstrate how to determine if a proposed discrepancy is inconclusive because the measurement is too noisy or ill-posed. We validate PIVOT on seismic imaging and real-world black hole imaging problems, where we find that OOD observations generally lead to larger perturbation strengths when the proposed discrepancy family captures relevant components of the mismatch, as long as the discrepancy is visible to the measurement. PIVOT thereby provides an interpretable probe into how real-world priors could be misspecified.

2605.11497.title: PoseBridge: Bridging the Skeletonization Gap for Zero-Shot Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
2605.11497.authors: Sanghyeon Lee, Jinwoo Kim, Jong Taek Lee
2605.11497.abstract: Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition (ZSSAR) is typically treated as a skeleton-text alignment problem: encode joint-coordinate sequences, align them with language, and classify unseen actions. We argue that this alignment is often too late. Skeletons are not complete action observations, but compressed outputs of human pose estimation (HPE); by the time alignment begins, human-object interactions and pose-relative visual cues may no longer be explicit. We call this upstream semantic loss. To address it, we propose PoseBridge, an HPE-aware ZSSAR framework that bridges intermediate HPE representations to skeleton-text alignment. Rather than adding an RGB action branch or object detector, PoseBridge extracts pose-anchored semantic cues from the same HPE process that produces skeletons, then transfers them through skeleton-conditioned bridging and semantic prototype adaptation. Across NTU-RGB+D 60/120, PKU-MMD, and Kinetics-200/400, PoseBridge improves ZSSAR performance under the evaluated protocols. On the Kinetics-200/400 PURLS benchmark, which contains in-the-wild videos with diverse scenes and action contexts, PoseBridge achieves substantial gains over prior ZSSAR methods, outperforming the strongest compared baseline by 13.3-17.4 points across all eight splits. Code is available at https://github.com/hyeon0819/PoseBridge.

2605.15923.title: Invaria: Learning Scale and Density Invariance in Point Clouds via Next-Resolution Prediction
2605.15923.authors: Chun-Peng Chang, Shaoxiang Wang, Alain Pagani, Dariu Gavrila, Holger Caesar
2605.15923.abstract: Modern image encoders achieve high generalization by decoupling semantic meaning from resolution, an ability yet to be fully realized in the 3D domain. We investigate the failure of 3D point cloud encoders to achieve similar generalization and find that existing models are highly sensitive to sampling resolution and scale changes, leading to significant performance degradation. This sensitivity is a major bottleneck for real-world deployment in robotics, as it suggests models overfit to specific quantization densities and object scales rather than learning invariant semantic features. To mitigate this dependency, we propose Invaria, a point cloud encoder that achieves scale and density invariance through next-resolution prediction and receptive field calibration. While our objective is not the explicit generation of high-resolution point clouds, we find that this training objective encourages the model to learn robust, structural invariants. The resulting encoder achieves significant performance gains during resolution shifts while maintaining high efficiency through a compact model size and reduced token requirements. Specifically, on ScanNet, Invaria achieves a 56.0\% higher mIoU at 3$\times$ lower resolution and a 20\% improvement when the objects scale is reduced by a factor of 3. These gains are achieved with a 45\% smaller model size and an average reduction of 40\% in input tokens.

2605.16582.title: ArtMesh: Part-Aware Articulated Mesh Fields with Motion-Consistent Dynamics
2605.16582.authors: Sylvia Yuan, Dan Wang, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Xinrui Cui
2605.16582.abstract: We present ArtMesh, a mesh-native method for reconstructing articulated objects explicitly as connected triangle meshes with per-part rigid motion from multi-view observations in start and end states. Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines for articulated reconstruction inherit the unstructured point-based geometry of their splatting base, which provides no surface topology for reasoning about part boundaries or enforcing motion consistency along the object's connectivity. ArtMesh instead builds on a mesh-based differentiable rendering backbone, enabling part-aware dynamics to act directly on the structured topology. To make the topology compatible with articulation, we introduce part-aware restricted Delaunay remeshing, producing connected submeshes whose triangles do not cross semantic part boundaries. The dynamic mesh field then optimizes articulation using bidirectional Vertex-wise Motion Consistency on transported mesh vertices and Pixel-wise Motion Consistency on rendered images. We introduce Articulate-100, a new benchmark of 100 articulated objects spanning 16 PartNet-Mobility categories. On this benchmark, given ground-truth part masks, ArtMesh achieves the best aggregate joint-axis estimation and part-level geometric reconstruction among prior 3DGS-based pipelines, with the largest gains on objects with many movable parts.

2605.17620.title: SynVA: A Modular Toolkit for Vessel Generation and Aneurysm Editing
2605.17620.authors: Marten J. Finck, Niklas C. Koser, Sarker M. Mahfuz, Tameem Jahangir, Jon E. Wilhelm, Daniel Behme, Naomi Larsen, Wojtek Palubicki, Sylvia Saalfeld, S\"oren Pirk
2605.17620.abstract: Intracranial aneurysms (IAs), characterized by unpredictable growth and risk of rupture, are a major cause of stroke and can lead to life-threatening hemorrhages with high mortality and long-term disability. With aging populations, the incidence and overall burden of cerebrovascular diseases are expected to increase, highlighting the need for scalable approaches to analyze complex medical data and improve population-level understanding of these conditions. While digital twins and deep learning offer promising avenues for improving diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, their effectiveness is limited by the scarcity of large-scale, high-quality medical data and corresponding labels. We present Synthetic VAsculature (SynVA), a modular toolkit for vascular mesh generation and anatomically consistent aneurysm synthesis. SynVA combines novel flow-matching-based methods for generating healthy vessel meshes with learning-based approaches for anatomy-conditioned aneurysm mesh generation; it computes aneurysms from pre-existing vascular geometries rather than generating them in isolation. In addition, we introduce the SynVA procedural model for vascular and aneurysm synthesis based solely on physiological principles and statistical priors, which enables the generation of large-scale datasets. To this end, we release a dataset of 50,000 fully labeled mesh samples for a variety of downstream vision tasks. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations show that SynVA generates realistic vessel geometries and anatomically plausible aneurysms, with only minor trade-offs between expert-perceived realism and similarity to real aneurysms. Moreover, pretraining on SynVA data improves point-cloud segmentation and morphological parameter estimation on real data. Code will be released upon acceptance.

2605.21171.title: FTerViT: Fully Ternary Vision Transformer
2605.21171.authors: Szymon Ruci\'nski, Pietro Bonazzi, Engin T\"uretken, Simon Narduzzi, Michele Magno, Nadim Maamari
2605.21171.abstract: Ternary Vision Transformers offer substantial model compression, however state-of-the-art methods only ternarize the encoder layers, leaving patch embeddings, LayerNorm parameters, and classifier heads in full precision. In compact models targeting resource-constrained processors, such as microcontrollers, these remaining full-precision components determine the total memory footprint, severely limiting deployment efficiency and on-device feasibility. In this work, we introduce a fully ternarized Vision Transformer in which all weight matrices and normalization parameters are ternarized, while activations remain 8-bit (FTerViT). To this end, we introduce two novel operators: TernaryBitConv2d with per-channel scaling for patch embedding and TernaryLayerNorm. FTerViT is trained using knowledge distillation, followed by a lightweight quantization-aware recovery phase. On a matched DeiT-S backbone, FTerViT reaches 77.47% ImageNet-1K top-1 at 5.81 MB, +3.27 pp over TerViT. With the stronger DeiT-III-S backbone at 384x384 resolution, our ternary W2A8 model achieves 82.43% at 6.09 MB (~15x compression, -2.42 pp vs. FP32). This backbone- and resolution-advantaged result exceeds prior ternary ViTs by up to 8 pp. Finally, we demonstrate the first implementation of ternary vision transformers on a dual-core Xtensa LX7 microcontroller inside the ESP32-S3 system-on-chip. By deploying FTerViT-Small (based on DeiT-III-Small at 224x224 resolution, 5.81 MB), we achieve 79.64% ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy.

2605.25759.title: Towards Anatomically Plausible Human Image Generation via Synthetic Localized Preferences
2605.25759.authors: Bao Li, Yuliang Xiu, Zhen Liu
2605.25759.abstract: Large-scale text-to-image foundation models have achieved remarkable visual realism, yet generating human images with correct anatomical structures remains challenging. Existing approaches enforce anatomical constraints through part-specific modules or localized loss weighting during supervised fine-tuning on high-quality human photos, but such datasets are limited and often provide ambiguous optimization signals due to confounding factors such as lighting, pose, and background. Preference-based alignment offers an alternative, but standard Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) treats all pixels equally and therefore fails to exploit the localized nature of anatomical artifacts. To address this, we propose the framework of Alignment via Synthetic Anatomical Preference (ASAP), which constructs controlled preference pairs through a localized degradation mechanism applied to high-fidelity human images. This mechanism performs a controlled experiment on images by introducing explicit anatomical errors in targeted regions while preserving the remaining content. With this mechanism, we create the Human Anatomical Preference (HAP) dataset with over 10K curated pairs for effective anatomical alignment of text-to-image human image generative models. To better leverage the locality of these controlled preference pairs, we introduce a localized and margin-bounded variant of DPO that prioritizes optimization in targeted anatomical regions while enforcing a finite preference margin to prevent over-optimization and preserve global semantics. We further introduce HAF-Bench, a benchmark for systematic evaluation of anatomical fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ASAP consistently reduces anatomical errors across multiple foundation models while maintaining overall image quality.

2605.28551.title: Resolution-free neural surrogates for geometric parameterization and mapping with spatially varying fields
2605.28551.authors: Yanwen Huang, Lok Ming Lui, Gary P. T. Choi
2605.28551.abstract: Many imaging problems require computing spatial transformations induced by spatially varying intensity, feature, or density fields. Canonical examples include distortion correction, deformable image registration, atlas-based segmentation, and deformation-driven image analysis. These tasks can be formulated as geometric mapping problems in which the transformation is constrained to preserve local structure, control boundary behavior, or regulate angular distortion. Such formulations typically lead to variational models, diffusion processes, or elliptic partial differential equations. However, repeatedly solving high-resolution systems becomes computationally expensive when the underlying parameter fields vary across instances. In this work, we propose a resolution-free neural surrogate for geometric parameterization and mapping problems. Given a spatially varying parameter field $p:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^m$ and grid nodes $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N\subset\Omega$, the model predicts mapped locations $\{u(x_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ on structured grids of different sizes without retraining. To avoid dependence on a fixed grid, we use a multi-resolution geometric encoding strategy that conditions the network on coordinate-augmented samples of the parameter field. The model is trained without labeled solution data by enforcing geometry-aware constraints derived from variational energies, diffusion-based density equalization, and quasi-conformal theory. Experimental results on quasi-conformal mapping and density-equalizing mapping problems are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

2605.30894.title: SteerFace: Debiasing Synthetic Face Generation via Adaptive Residue Perturbation
2605.30894.authors: Yuxi Mi, Qiuyang Yuan, Jianqing Xu, Yichun Zhou, Xuan Zhao, Jun Wang, Rizen Guo, Shuigeng Zhou
2605.30894.abstract: The shortage of legally compliant data for face recognition training has sparked growing interest in using synthetic data as an alternative. While recent diffusion-based methods enable the generation of photorealistic face images with strong identity adherence and data diversity, their downstream recognition performance still exhibits a significant synthetic-real gap. This paper identifies visual tendency as a previously underexplored limitation, whereby synthetic data exhibit an unrealistic prevalence of visual attributes and thus deviate from the real-data distribution. Visual tendency can be attributed to the generator's conditioning on identity embeddings, through which co-occurring residual visual cues are unintentionally absorbed into learned identity semantics. To discourage the generator from exploiting such visual cues, this paper proposes SteerFace, a simple and efficient training framework that perturbs identity embeddings by steering them toward random orthogonal directions on the embedding hypersphere. The perturbation serves as an identity-preserving regularizer that penalizes the generator's reliance on non-identity components, as supported by theoretical analysis. This paper further introduces an adaptive strategy that learns perturbation strengths with both sample-wise preference and favorable overall statistics. Extensive experiments show that SteerFace effectively mitigates visual tendency, outperforms prior methods in downstream face recognition, and generalizes well across different training datasets and generation pipelines.

2606.11390.title: Large-Scale Gaussian Splatting with a Multi-GPU PyTorch Backend
2606.11390.authors: Matthew Cong, Francis Williams, Jonathan Swartz, Mark Harris, Sanja Fidler, Ken Museth
2606.11390.abstract: Gaussian splatting methods have become increasingly popular for neural reconstruction of the real world. However, they are often limited in scale and resolution due to compute and memory constraints. We present a multi-GPU Gaussian splatting approach that scales reconstruction to higher resolutions and larger scenes while abstracting away the code complexity typically associated with distributing a model. We demonstrate city-scale reconstructions with street-level detail consisting of over 1 billion Gaussian splats. To accomplish this, we propose a PyTorch backend that distributes parameters and operators across GPUs via CUDA unified memory, with optional NVLink support. Because distribution occurs at the operator level, the model code requires no explicit cross-device communication. More broadly, the backend exposes multiple GPUs as an aggregate asynchronous PyTorch device and supports a broad set of PyTorch operators enabling the distribution of general PyTorch workloads.

2607.04882.title: Unsupervised Detection of Underground Tunnels in Ground-Penetrating Radar Using Depth-Restricted Reconstruction Scoring
2607.04882.authors: Muhammad Junaid, Shoab A. Khan, Nisar Ahmed
2607.04882.abstract: Hand-dug tunnels that reach buried pipelines from below are hard to find before they are used, and too rare to train a supervised detector. The engineering application of this work is detecting such tunnels in ground-penetrating radar surveys of a monitored site. The contribution in artificial intelligence is a detection scheme that needs no tunnel examples: a convolutional autoencoder learns the site's normal ground from surveys recorded before any tunnel exists, later survey windows are scored by their largest reconstruction errors within the travel-time band where a tunnel can lie, and evaluation holds out whole survey lines. On field data from a tunnel hand-dug for this study (0.6 m wide, 1 m high, roof 0.9-1.4 m deep) and surveyed repeatedly with a 250-megahertz radar in dry and wet conditions, the detector reaches an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.994 and an F1 score of 0.972 on 1,600 test windows and flags all 29 tunnel crossings. Restricting the score to the depth band improves all six detectors tested and, with a quarter of the training data, outperforms whole-window scoring trained on all of it; the best rule for the same band without learning misses 9 of the 29 crossings. On two unseen plots, false alarms stay at 1.6% on comparable ground but reach 9.3% on irrigated soil; recalibrating the threshold on a fifth of that plot's lines lowers them to 4.2%, retraining brings no significant further reduction, and models trained there alone still detect the original tunnel.

2607.14726.title: AE-UAV: An Air-to-Air Event Camera Dataset for UAV Detection and Tracking with Continuous-Time Annotations
2607.14726.authors: Zixin Jiang, Bing He, Chaoran Xiong, Zhenzhen Wang, Xin Zhao, Ling Pei
2607.14726.abstract: Perceiving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from another UAV is essential for aerial avoidance, interception, and counter-UAV operations. Event cameras suit this task because of their microsecond temporal resolution and high dynamic range. However, existing event-based UAV datasets were mostly recorded by static or ground-based observers, and their targets are annotated only at fixed frame rates. We present AE-UAV, an air-to-air event camera dataset collected from a flying UAV for detection and tracking. It contains 178 sequences of event data at 1280x720 resolution covering daytime and nighttime flights under three motion geometries. A continuous-time annotation framework based on cubic B-spline interpolation provides ground-truth boxes at arbitrary timestamps and a label for every event. Hold-out experiments confirm a median interpolation error of 2.19 pixels, reducing the piecewise-constant baseline error by 74\%. We benchmark six detectors and six trackers across illumination and motion conditions. The results show that nighttime and head-on scenarios are the hardest cases for detectors. A cross-rate generalization study further shows that learned trackers lose their accuracy when the test aggregation rate differs from the training rate. The dataset will be publicly released at https://github.com/MSP-xEN/AE-UAV.

2607.19986.title: STEREOFLOW: Progressive Stereo Matching with StereoDiT and Transition Flow Matching
2607.19986.authors: Hao Wang, Haoran Geng, Xiaotong Yang, Jing Tang, Songlin Wei, Linlong Lang, Yeying Jin, Zheng Zhu, Zhaoxin Fan, Biao Leng
2607.19986.abstract: Stereo matching is a fundamental task in 3D reconstruction. Despite remarkable advances, the prevailing paradigms formulate stereo matching as a deterministic regression problem, collapsing the multimodal distribution modeling into a single-point estimation. This formulation suffers from a regression-to-mean bias, frequently struggling with ambiguous regions. In contrast, we introduce a prior-guided generative framework that integrates deterministic matching regression and generative distribution modeling within a complementary formulation. Built upon this formulation, we introduce StereoFlow through three key components: (i) a two-stage progressive cascade matching network that progressively produces multi-resolution stereo conditions with complementary matching cues; (ii) a pixel diffusion transformer (termed StereoDiT) with a frequency-decoupled architecture for modeling correspondence ambiguity; (iii) a few-step flow matching objective (termed Transition Flow Matching) for efficient optimization. In summary, \textsc{\textbf{StereoFlow}} achieves strong geometric consistency and rich fine-grained details in ill-posed, discontinuous regions and under zero-shot generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed StereoFlow establishes multiple state-of-the-art results across benchmarks, including Scene Flow, KITTI, ETH3D, and Middlebury.

2607.24981.title: Enabling Fully Integer-Only Inference for Lightweight Detection Transformers
2607.24981.authors: Thanh Cong Le, Michal Szczepanski, Martyna Poreba
2607.24981.abstract: Vision Transformer detectors now approach the accuracy of CNNs but remain difficult to deploy on NPUs and microcontrollers because key components, including deformable attention, feature fusion, and nonlinear activation functions, are not natively compatible with integer arithmetic. Existing quantized detectors either retain operators such as Softmax, GELU, and LayerNorm or focus on heavyweight backbones, leaving lightweight detection transformers without an end-to-end integer implementation. We address this gap with I-LW-DETR, the first fully integer-only lightweight DETR, in which every operation in the forward pass, including transformer nonlinearities, is executed in integer arithmetic. I-LW-DETR is built upon three key components: a scale-preserving split convolution that assigns independent activation scale to each branch of the multi-scale projector; SD-ShiftGELU, a sign-dependent GELU approximation that preserves element-wise behavior while avoiding the accuracy degradation; and a constrained Shiftmax that maintains stable Softmax normalization. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed quantization pipeline consistently produces efficient fully integer-only models across different model scales. Across all model scales, the proposed pipeline incurs only a moderate accuracy degradation while reducing the model size by approximately $3.6\times$ and the computational cost by more than one order of magnitude.

2608.12313.title: AVA-Encoder: Learning to Represent Videos via Reconstruction-Driven Agentic Self-Evolution
2608.12313.authors: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang, Bingnan Li, Yining Zhao, Shuqi Gu, Kan Ren, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Huang
2608.12313.abstract: Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video "Auto-Encoder" (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from human films, turning them into agent-native video representations with reconstruction itself as the sole supervision. It encodes a film into a Film Knowledge Graph (Film KG) of structured-text nodes, typed dependency edges, and linked multimodal assets, then regenerates the film from this graph with a fixed decoder. Crucially, by distilling reconstruction residuals into textual gradients, AVA-Encoder drives a dual-loop self-evolution: an outer loop autonomously discovers a generalizable encoding strategy entirely from unlabeled videos, while an inner loop refines each video's Film KG at test time. AVA-Encoder improves reconstruction fidelity by 20.9 percentage points over the strongest baseline, and its autonomously learned strategy outperforms a human-tuned strategy using 70% fewer prompt tokens. Our representations drive three downstream breakthroughs: (1) Film KGs enable coordinated graph-based editing and (2) improve one-shot video generation across four open-source frameworks, while (3) fine-tuning agents on our reverse-engineered trajectories boosts video creation quality by 38.7%. We release the framework and a dataset of 500 Film KGs with over 27,000 creation trajectories.

2608.24646.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models
2608.24646.authors: Wei Zhou, Xiongwei Zhu, Lingdong Kong, Bo Chen, Lei Zhang, Yongyuan Liang, Xiaoxia Hou, Tian Ye, Xian Sun, Yingshuo Wang, Linfeng Li, Shengqiong Wu, Leigang Qu, Feng Li, Wei Liu, Julian McAuley, Tat-Seng Chua
2608.24646.abstract: Reinforcement learning aligns diffusion and flow models with human preferences and task objectives, yet endpoint rewards do not specify how an intermediate denoising prediction should change. We introduce DiffusionOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework that converts image-level reward guidance into explicit self-teachers for clean-output predictions at sampled on-policy queries. At each outer iteration, a frozen exponential moving average self-teacher rolls out trajectories to supply low-noise query states and clean-output anchors. Normalized local reward gradients then synthesize bounded positive and negative self-teachers around each anchor. The student policy distills these detached self-teachers under a finite update budget before an online update refreshes the self-teacher, admitting an exact single-branch variant DiffusionOPSD*. Separating self-teacher synthesis from student backpropagation removes the decoder and reward model from student backward passes and makes synthesis and realized gains separately measurable. On SD3.5-M and step-distilled Z-Image-Turbo, DiffusionOPSD and DiffusionOPSD* achieve the best held-out score across all 20 target-reward settings, winning 19 of 20 individually with gains up to 44.0% over the strongest baseline. They also deliver up to 2.57% the base-anchored gain of ReFL and up to 90% single-reward human win rates, while joint multi-reward training transfers zero-shot with up to 81% human win rates. Separately, comprehensive profiling experiments show that DiffusionOPSD and DiffusionOPSD* use up to 63% and 74% fewer GPU-hours per 100 updates than DiffusionNFT and reach baseline terminal quality up to 13.1% faster. Overall, DiffusionOPSD provides a teacher-free paradigm converting rewards into stable intermediate supervision for diffusion post-training.

2608.24845.title: LAION-BVD: A 13-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
2608.24845.authors: Andreas Hochlehnert, Marianna Nezhurina, Mehdi Cherti, Andrej Radonjic, Thadd\"aus Wiedemer, Christoph Schuhmann, Romain Beaumont, Wieland Brendel, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, A. Sophia Koepke, Jenia Jitsev, Matthias Bethge
2608.24845.abstract: We present LAION-BVD (LAION - Big Video Dataset), a large-scale open video dataset for multimodal learning, which contains 1.3B platform-specific video URLs collected from CommonCrawl. From these, we download 80M videos with a total duration of 13.5 million hours. The dataset is designed for multimodal pre-training across the video, audio, and image modalities. Using content-aware scene detection, we extract clips for which we synthetically generate video and audio captions. Models trained on these data achieve competitive performance on standard video-text and audio-text benchmarks, with consistent improvements as training or model scale increases. Additionally, we explore video frames as an alternative source of image-text data by extracting scene-changing frames. These frames exhibit a visual distribution distinct from standard web image corpora, and models trained on this dataset achieve strong image-text retrieval performance. We release LAION-BVD to the research community. It significantly expands open access to multimodal videos at an unprecedented scale.

2608.29269.title: LightFuse: Relightable Interactive Gaussian Scene Reconstruction via Multi-Scan Fusion and 2D Gaussian Ray Tracing
2608.29269.authors: Haonan Zhou, Gaoxiang Linghu, Youlin Jia, Chuanyu Cheng, Hongyu Cui, Kewei Wei, Bruce X. B. Yu, Gaoang Wang
2608.29269.abstract: Relightable interactive scene reconstruction aims to build an editable 3D model from scans of different object arrangements, so that novel layouts can be rendered under novel illumination. However, Gaussian-splatting-based methods bake illumination into appearance and thus cannot jointly reconstruct scans captured under different lighting, while existing multi-illumination inverse rendering methods struggle to handle scenes whose geometry changes across captures. We present LightFuse, a 2D Gaussian inverse rendering framework that bridges this gap by extending interactive scene reconstruction with explicit material-illumination decomposition and physically based relighting. LightFuse fuses observations across states to reconstruct a shared background and movable objects. Since geometry optimized by splatting alone is ill-suited for ray-tracing-based inverse rendering, it then performs ray-tracing-oriented geometry refinement to obtain more complete and consistent surfaces. Because rearrangement leaves materials unchanged, we jointly optimize a shared set of materials across all scans under varying illumination, with differentiable one-bounce ray tracing disentangling them from the per-scan environment lighting. Experiments on novel-state relighting of synthetic scenes and novel-state synthesis of captured real scenes show that LightFuse outperforms interactive reconstruction and adapted inverse rendering baselines, improving novel-state relighting PSNR by 6.01 dB over the strongest baseline and achieving the highest PSNR on captured scenes. Project page: https://zhn202.github.io/LightFuse/ .

2609.13043.title: Unified CT and MRI Pancreas Segmentation for Label-Efficient Cross-Modality Subregion Transfer
2609.13043.authors: Ziliang Hong, Hongyi Pan, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Andrea Bejar, Elif Keles, Frank H. Miller, Michael B. Wallace, Rajesh N. Keswani, Gorkem Durak, Alpay Medetalibeyoglu, Candice Bolan, Zongwei Zhou, Ulas Bagci
2609.13043.abstract: Robust medical image segmentation across imaging modalities is challenging because of large differences in appearance and intensity distributions. Models trained on a single modality often show substantial performance drops when applied to unseen domains. In this work, we develop a unified 3D pancreas segmentation framework that applies domain-adversarial learning to 4,604 heterogeneous CT and MRI scans to learn anatomical representations. A shared nnU-Net encoder-decoder is trained for whole-pancreas segmentation, with a latent domain discriminator encouraging CT-MRI feature alignment. The learned encoder is subsequently transferred to pancreatic head-body-tail segmentation using limited MRI-only subregion annotations. An average Dice score of 87.31% on the in-distribution test set and Dice scores ranging from 84.20% to 88.09% across external OOD datasets were achieved in whole pancreas segmentation. Dice scores of 80.53% on MRI and 83.05% on CT were achieved for downstream subregion segmentation, without using CT subregion annotations. These results demonstrate that a unified anatomical representation can support both cross-modality pancreas segmentation and label-efficient downstream transfer.

2609.13259.title: TryOnReward: Learning Foveated Consistency for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Virtual Try-On
2609.13259.authors: Xueheng Li, Yong Liu, Xiaolong Fu, Wen Xue, Chengjun Xie, Yipeng Sun, Yan Li, Simiu Gu
2609.13259.abstract: Virtual Try-On (VTON) aims to dress a person with the reference garment, producing visually reasonable results aligned with human preferences. Turning this preference-oriented goal into an actionable objective relies on a scoring function aligned with human taste.
